submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad sequence-start head with a full-stop bonus: its write only gets far from its mean when its attention stays concentrated on a few tokens, which happens at the opening of a text (median strength 0.25 of max on the 2nd token, 0.20 on the 3rd, 0.17 on the 4th, and under 0.14 from about the 6th token on) and on a full stop '.' or '。' (or an opening ' (' or '[' in the first ~6 positions), each of which takes 0.3-0.7 of the head's own attention. A full stop makes it strong (0.35-0.85 of max) and is the peak of about 6 in 10 punctuated 48-token texts, holding above the line to about position 25-30 and falling below it after ~position 40; commas, colons, semicolons, digits, space-prefixed closers ' )' and ordinary words past the 4th position stay below the line, except that code or repetitive technical text can hold weak runs (0.25-0.45 of max) because adjacent punctuation keeps the attention concentrated.

rival_explanations: A pure token-class reading: the head is a clause-final punctuation detector whose strength does not depend on position, so it predicts an opening ' (' or a period at position 20 is as strong as one at position 2.

An attention-sink reading: the head only reacts to being near the start of a sequence and has no token preference at all, so it predicts a period at position 30 is inactive and that the peak always sits on the 2nd or 3rd token.

A copy/salience reading: the head fires whenever its attention concentrates on any high-write content token, so it predicts code and repetitive technical text are broadly active (0.3-0.5 of max) regardless of punctuation and that plain-prose periods are no stronger than content-word runs.
